app.needRepo: Connect a repository to fix first and you can install. The app attaches to that one repository only.
app.lostNote: Reinstalling picks up where it left off. In the meantime it tries with the token below or the shared Feedloop account.
app.lostFallback: Please check the GitHub app connection
app.unbindNote: Unlinking leaves the installation on the GitHub side. To remove it completely, uninstall it in the installation settings.
app.title: Feedloop app installation
app.prOpened: PRs are opened as {login}. There is no token to create or renew.
app.allRepos: This installation can reach every repository on the account. You can narrow it to “Only select repositories” in GitHub installation settings.
app.installExplain: Click install to go to GitHub; you come back automatically. On that screen, pick just the one repository to fix and click Install, and you are done: there is no token to create, copy and paste. PRs are opened as {login}. The permissions are read/write on that repository's Contents and Pull requests, and read on Deployments and Commit statuses. If you already installed Feedloop on this account (for another service), click Connect next to it.

broad.note: It works fine, but if it leaks the damage reaches further. We recommend switching to a fine-grained token (github_pat_…) limited to this repository.
broad.title: This token can reach every repository on the account{scopes}

token.label: GitHub token
token.removeNote: Removing it returns to the shared account. PRs cannot be created on repositories it has not been invited to.
token.removeNoteApp: Removing it leaves the app installation as is. You only lose PRs on repositories the app cannot reach.

steps.s1: In <link>GitHub › Settings › Developer settings › Fine-grained tokens</link> click “Generate new token”. This link opens with the name, permissions and expiry prefilled
steps.s2: Set Repository access to Only select repositories and pick {repo, select, none {only the repository to fix} other {only {repo}}}
steps.s3: Under Permissions › Repository permissions, set Contents and Pull requests to Read and write
steps.s4: (Optional) Give Deployments and Commit statuses Read access and the Fix PRs screen also shows preview and build status. Without them only that field shows “Unknown”
steps.s5: It must be a repository you own or are a member of. A repository you were only invited to as a collaborator does not work with a fine-grained token and needs a classic token (ghp_)
steps.pasteNote: Before saving, we check with GitHub {repo, select, has {that the token can access this repository} other {that the token is valid}}. Write access is judged on the first PR. The token is stored encrypted and only the last 4 characters stay on screen.

failedNote: The token may have expired or the repository permissions may have changed. Replacing it with a new token clears this notice.

alt.hintNoApp: We recommend installing the app above. Add a token only if organization policy prevents installing the app.
alt.hintApp: When the app is installed it takes priority. The token is only used for repositories the app cannot reach (older PRs) or when the app does not work.
alt.title: Connect with your own token (alternative)

summary.noConnection: Without a connection, PRs cannot be created.
summary.noRepo: There is no repository to fix yet. Once you register one, PRs are opened on it.
summary.app: Right now the Feedloop app creates branches and PRs as {login, select, none {the bot} other {{login}}}.
summary.token: Right now branches and PRs are created from your GitHub account.
summary.shared: Without a connection, Feedloop tries with the shared Feedloop account. That only works on repositories that account was invited to as a collaborator. Connect below and PRs open on your repository directly, with no invitation.

status.tokenRemoved: Token removed. Feedloop will now try with the shared account
status.tokenSavedNoRepo: Token verified and saved. Once you connect a repository, PRs are opened from this account
status.tokenSaved: Token verified and saved. PRs are opened from this account from now on
status.unbound: Unlinked. The installation on the GitHub side is still there

errors.networkSave: Could not save because of a network error
errors.networkCheck: Could not check because of a network error

loadError: Could not load the GitHub connection settings. Please reload.

recheck.unknown: Could not read the check result. Please try again in a moment
recheck.changed: This repository has a different installation. Use “Reinstall” to link it to this bot
recheck.suspended: The app is suspended. Lift the suspension in GitHub installation settings
recheck.missing: Could not find the Feedloop app installation on this repository. Please install it again
recheck.notBound: It is not linked to this bot yet. Start the installation with the button above
recheck.noRepo: There is no repository to fix, so there is nothing to check. Connect a repository first
recheck.ok: The installation is still there. PRs can be opened on this repository

footer.app: PRs created by the {service} bot are opened as {login}.
footer.token: PRs created by the {service} bot are opened under the name of this token's account.
footer.merge: Merging is still done by a person, in Feedloop's “Fix PRs” screen or on GitHub.

callback.bound: GitHub app installed and linked to this bot
callback.no_repo: Connect a repository to fix first. Install after that and it links
callback.not_installed: Installed, but this bot's repository is not on the app's access list. Add the repository in GitHub installation settings
callback.suspended: The app is suspended on GitHub. Lift the suspension in installation settings
callback.no_push: The GitHub account that installed it has no write access to this repository. Install it with the repository owner or an account with write access
callback.unknown_push: Could not check with GitHub. Click “Check installation” in a moment
callback.requested: An install request was sent to the organization owner. Once it is approved, click the install button once more to connect
callback.need_state: Could not tell which service to connect. Start again with “Install” on Feedloop's connect screen (if it is already installed, it only checks and returns right away)
callback.no_code: Did not receive the authorization needed to connect. Start again with the install button
callback.auth_failed: GitHub authorization check failed. Start again with the install button
callback.no_bot: There is no service to connect. Register a service first, then install
callback.unconfigured: The GitHub app is not set up on this deployment. Connect with a token instead
callback.busy: Too many install requests. Please try again in a moment
callback.error: Something went wrong while connecting. Try again with the install button in a moment
